submitted.rationale: Index 10 (Bi0.436 V0.564) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 2.33e-5 A. It is slightly V-rich BiVO4, the strongest-performing phase in this system. The foundation-model checks agree: MACE puts BiVO4 0.008 eV/atom above the hull, and MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of 2.99 eV, below the 3.22 eV photons. Photocurrent peaked at V≈0.56 and fell on both sides.

rejected.reason: Measured 5.3e-6 A. Near stoichiometric BiVO4, but about 4x lower than index 10.
Measured 1.41e-5 A. More V-rich than index 10 and already past the optimum.
Not measured. The trend points toward the V-rich side, and Bi-rich films form Bi4V2O11/Bi2O3-type phases, which are generally weaker photoanodes.

consultations.verdict: Support: BiVO4 (mp-23506) is near-hull (0.008 eV/atom) with HSE gap ~3.0 eV < 3.22 eV photon energy, so it absorbs. Index 14 (Bi 0.49) is closest to BiVO4 stoichiometry.
Mildly supportive: V2O5 secondary phase (gap ~2.8 eV) would also absorb and may form a BiVO4/V2O5 heterojunction; index 10 is slightly V-rich BiVO4, a reasonable probe of the V-rich side of the peak.
Support: V2O5 is on hull, so V-rich compositions are two-phase BiVO4+V2O5; the measured trend (V 0.51 -> 0.56 increased photocurrent 4x) favors the most V-rich candidate, index 4 (V 0.571).
